components.note: 亻 (person) — marks people, as in 你, 他, 们; 伊 is a literary she/he and a name syllable.
尹 (yǐn) is only a loose sound hint for yī.
丽 (beautiful) — simplified 麗, which showed a deer 鹿 with antlers, a symbol of grace. Seen in 美丽.
艹 (plants) — marks grasses, as in 花, 草, 茶; 莎 is a sedge grass, seen in 莎士比亚 Shakespeare.
沙 (shā) gives the sound: 莎 shā, also in 纱 shā and 鲨 shā.
白 (white, bright) — gives sound to 拍 pāi, 怕 pà, 伯 bó and 泊 bó. Meaning: white, clear, plain, hence "明白" understand.

example.hanzi: 伊丽莎白是这个小镇上最受欢迎的老师。
example.pinyin: yīlìshābái shì zhège xiǎozhèn shàng zuì shòu huānyíng de lǎoshī.
example.english: Elizabeth is the most popular teacher in this small town.
example.fact: Queen Elizabeth II reigned for over 70 years, longer than any other British monarch, and during her lifetime she met more than half of all US presidents ever elected, from Harry Truman through Joe Biden.

examples.hanzi: 伊丽莎白昨天给我发了一封邮件。
examples.pinyin: Yīlìshābái zuótiān gěi wǒ fā le yì fēng yóujiàn.
examples.english: Elizabeth sent me an email yesterday.

examples.hanzi: 伊丽莎白打算明年去中国学习。
examples.pinyin: Yīlìshābái dǎsuàn míngnián qù Zhōngguó xuéxí.
examples.english: Elizabeth plans to study in China next year.

components.note: 去 (to go) — 丢 looks like 去 with an extra stroke on top. Memory aid: something that 'goes' away is lost.
厶 (private, small) — the lower part, as in 去. The dictionary story (a lost piece of jade 玉) is a later reading, not proven.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.hanzi: 在这么多人面前摔倒真是太丢人了。
example.pinyin: zài zhème duō rén miànqián shuāidǎo zhēnshi tài diūrén le.
example.english: Falling in front of so many people is really embarrassing.
example.fact: Blushing is the only human expression that Charles Darwin himself called 'the most peculiar and most human of all expressions' — unlike most emotional reactions, it can't be consciously suppressed, because it's controlled by the sympathetic nervous system rather than muscles we can voluntarily control.

examples.hanzi: 迟到太丢人了，我不好意思进去。
examples.pinyin: Chídào tài diūrén le, wǒ bù hǎoyìsi jìnqù.
examples.english: Being late is so embarrassing that I'm shy to go in.

examples.hanzi: 他不想在朋友面前丢人。
examples.pinyin: Tā bù xiǎng zài péngyou miànqián diūrén.
examples.english: He doesn't want to lose face in front of his friends.

components.note: 亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 作. 做 is a later variant of 作 zuò (to do), sharing its meaning and sound.
故 (gù) is only a loose sound hint.
彐 (hand-like part) — 事 is usually explained as a hand holding a tool or tally, 'handling business' — a hedged reading, not certain.
史 (history, scribe) — shares an ancient root with 事: a hand holding a recording tool. Both are about handling official 'matters'.

example.hanzi: 他做事一向很认真。
example.pinyin: tā zuòshì yīxiàng hěn rènzhēn.
example.english: He has always been very serious about handling matters.
example.fact: Henry Ford's moving assembly line, introduced in 1913, cut the time needed to build a Model T from about 12 hours to roughly 90 minutes, a leap in efficiency that transformed manufacturing worldwide and helped make car ownership affordable for millions.

examples.hanzi: 她在银行做事，每天九点上班。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài yínháng zuòshì, měi tiān jiǔ diǎn shàngbān.
examples.english: She works at a bank and starts at nine every day.

examples.hanzi: 他做事很有条理。
examples.pinyin: Tā zuòshì hěn yǒu tiáolǐ.
examples.english: He handles things in an orderly way.

components.note: 夂 (foot) — stopping or going: 处 first meant to stay or settle, then a place or to deal with.
土 (earth) — ground and place, as in 地 earth, 坐 sit; 在 is "to be at a place".
才 (cái) is a close sound clue for zài; 才 also appears in 材 cái.

example.hanzi: 这个国家目前正处在经济转型期。
example.pinyin: zhège guójiā mùqián zhèng chǔzài jīngjì zhuǎnxíng qī.
example.english: This country is currently in a period of economic transition.
example.fact: Istanbul is the only major city in the world situated on two continents, with the Bosphorus Strait splitting it between Europe and Asia — a geographic position that has made it a strategic crossroads for trade and empires for over 2,500 years.

examples.hanzi: 我们现在处在一个关键的时刻。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xiànzài chǔ zài yí ge guānjiàn de shíkè.
examples.english: We are now at a crucial moment.

examples.hanzi: 这座小镇处在两座山之间。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò xiǎozhèn chǔ zài liǎng zuò shān zhījiān.
examples.english: This small town lies between two mountains.

components.note: 贝 (cowry shell, money) — wealth and value: 财, 货, 买, 贵. 负 shows a person 人 carrying money: a burden, to bear or owe.
贝 (cowry shell, money) — 责 first meant demanding payment of a debt, hence duty. 责 sounds out 债 zhài, 积 jī and 绩 jì.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.hanzi: 请联系项目负责人确认时间。
example.pinyin: qǐng liánxì xiàngmù fùzérén quèrèn shíjiān.
example.english: Please contact the person in charge of the project to confirm the time.
example.fact: During the 1970 Apollo 13 crisis, flight director Gene Kranz — the person in charge of NASA's Mission Control — refused to accept that the crew could not be brought home safely, coordinating an improvised carbon-dioxide scrubber fix built entirely from materials already onboard the spacecraft.

examples.hanzi: 这个项目的负责人是王经理。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xiàngmù de fùzérén shì Wáng jīnglǐ.
examples.english: The person in charge of this project is Manager Wang.

examples.hanzi: 请问这里的负责人在吗？
examples.pinyin: Qǐngwèn zhèlǐ de fùzérén zài ma?
examples.english: Excuse me, is the person in charge here?

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 讠 is the simplified 言 (speech), as in 说, 话; 辩 puts two 辛 (offenders) with words between them, an argument.

example.hanzi: 他们在为这个问题争辩。
example.pinyin: Tāmen zài wèi zhège wèntí zhēngbiàn.
example.english: They are arguing about this problem.
example.fact: 辩 is argument in words: 辩论 (debate), 辩护 (to defend in court), 辩解 (to justify), 狡辩 (to quibble). Learners mix it up with 辨 (biàn, to distinguish); 辩 has the speech radical 讠, so it is about talking.

examples.hanzi: 他不想为自己辩解。
examples.pinyin: Tā bù xiǎng wèi zìjǐ biànjiě.
examples.english: He does not want to defend himself.

examples.hanzi: 两个同学在课堂上辩论。
examples.pinyin: Liǎng ge tóngxué zài kètáng shàng biànlùn.
examples.english: Two classmates are debating in class.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — marks actions done by hand, as in 打, 拉, 提; 撤 is to pull away. The right side matches old 徹 (now 彻 chè), which gave the sound.

example.hanzi: 警察要求大家马上撤离。
example.pinyin: Jǐngchá yāoqiú dàjiā mǎshàng chèlí.
example.english: The police asked everyone to evacuate immediately.
example.fact: 撤 means to pull back: 撤退 (retreat), 撤离 (to evacuate), 撤销 (to revoke), 撤职 (to dismiss from a post). In chat apps, 撤回 is the "recall" button that takes back a sent message.

examples.hanzi: 大雨来了，大家快撤到屋里。
examples.pinyin: Dàyǔ lái le, dàjiā kuài chè dào wū lǐ.
examples.english: The heavy rain is coming, so everyone move back inside.

examples.hanzi: 服务员把桌上的盘子撤走了。
examples.pinyin: Fúwùyuán bǎ zhuō shàng de pánzi chè zǒu le.
examples.english: The waiter cleared the plates from the table.

components.note: 犭 (animal, dog) — animals, as in 狗 dog, 猫 cat, 狂 wild: dogs guard.
讠 (speech) — words and law; 狱 first meant a lawsuit, then a prison.

example.hanzi: 他在狱中度过了三年。
example.pinyin: Tā zài yù zhōng dùguò le sān nián.
example.english: He spent three years in prison.
example.fact: 狱 originally meant a lawsuit, shown by two dogs barking at each other with words between them, and later became "prison." Common words: 监狱 (jail), 入狱 (to be jailed), 越狱 (jailbreak) and 地狱 (hell).

examples.hanzi: 那部电影讲的是一个人越狱的故事。
examples.pinyin: Nà bù diànyǐng jiǎng de shì yí ge rén yuèyù de gùshi.
examples.english: That movie is about a man who escapes from prison.

examples.hanzi: 他在监狱里读了很多书。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài jiānyù lǐ dú le hěn duō shū.
examples.english: He read many books in prison.

components.note: 小 (small) — three small dots, tiny grains. As a radical it appears in 少 few, 尖 sharp.
贝 (cowry shell, money) — money and trade: 财, 货, 买, 贵; 费 is a cost or fee.
弗 (fú) is close to fèi; same part in 沸 fèi.

example.hanzi: 在美国吃饭通常需要给小费。
example.pinyin: zài měiguó chīfàn tōngcháng xūyào gěi xiǎofèi.
example.english: When dining in the US, you usually need to give a tip.
example.fact: Tipping is believed to have originated in the taverns of 17th-century England, where patrons paid extra 'to insure promptness'; the custom later spread through Europe and was brought back to the United States by wealthy Americans returning from Grand Tours, though it remains far less common in many other countries today.

examples.hanzi: 服务很好，所以我多给了一些小费。
examples.pinyin: Fúwù hěn hǎo, suǒyǐ wǒ duō gěi le yìxiē xiǎofèi.
examples.english: The service was great, so I left a bigger tip.

examples.hanzi: 在中国的餐厅，一般不用给小费。
examples.pinyin: Zài Zhōngguó de cāntīng, yìbān bú yòng gěi xiǎofèi.
examples.english: In Chinese restaurants, you generally don't need to tip.

components.note: 木 (tree) — wood, as in 树, 林, 桌: 极 first meant a roof beam, the very top.
及 (jí) gives the exact sound; also in 级 jí and 吸 xī.
立 (to stand) — standing upright at the tip or end; also in 站 stand, 童 child.
耑 (duān) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 瑞 ruì.

example.hanzi: 沙漠地区的气温变化十分极端。
example.pinyin: shāmò dìqū de qìwēn biànhuà shífēn jíduān.
example.english: Temperature changes in desert regions are extremely extreme.
example.fact: The Lut Desert in Iran holds the record for the hottest land surface temperature ever measured by satellite, 80.8°C (177°F) in 2005, even though virtually no one lives there to experience it directly.

examples.hanzi: 极端天气越来越多了。
examples.pinyin: Jíduān tiānqì yuè lái yuè duō le.
examples.english: Extreme weather is becoming more common.

examples.hanzi: 这样做太极端了，不如想个折中的办法。
examples.pinyin: Zhèyàng zuò tài jíduān le, bùrú xiǎng ge zhézhōng de bànfǎ.
examples.english: Doing it this way is too extreme, so let's think of a compromise.

meanings: intern (esp. a student in practical training)

components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 字, 室: a house stocked with goods, so solid and real.
习 (practice) — simplified from 習, a young bird 羽 flapping its wings again and again to learn to fly.
土 (earth) — a green shoot pushing up from the ground: growth, birth, life. 生 also sounds out 性 xìng, 姓 xìng and 星 xīng.

example.hanzi: 这个暑假她在一家科技公司当实习生。
example.pinyin: zhège shǔjià tā zài yī jiā kējì gōngsī dāng shíxíshēng.
example.english: This summer she is interning at a tech company.
example.fact: The modern internship traces back to medieval guild apprenticeships, where young people trained for years under a master craftsman before being allowed to work independently — apprenticeships for goldsmiths in medieval London, for instance, could last as long as seven years.

examples.hanzi: 这家公司每年招聘十名实习生。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī měi nián zhāopìn shí míng shíxíshēng.
examples.english: This company hires ten interns each year.

examples.hanzi: 实习生的工作是整理资料。
examples.pinyin: Shíxíshēng de gōngzuò shì zhěnglǐ zīliào.
examples.english: The interns' job is to organize materials.

components.note: 从 (cóng) gives the exact sound and the idea: many people together make a cluster.
木 (tree) — two trees side by side make a grove or forest; compare 森 with three.

example.hanzi: 探险队深入丛林寻找失落的古城。
example.pinyin: tànxiǎnduì shēnrù cónglín xúnzhǎo shīluò de gǔchéng.
example.english: The expedition team went deep into the jungle looking for the lost ancient city.
example.fact: The Amazon rainforest covers less than 1% of Earth's land surface yet is home to roughly 10% of all known species, and scientists still discover new species there at a rate of about one every two days.

examples.hanzi: 丛林里到处是奇怪的鸟叫声。
examples.pinyin: Cónglín lǐ dàochù shì qíguài de niǎojiào shēng.
examples.english: The jungle is full of strange bird calls.

examples.hanzi: 他们在丛林里迷了路。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen zài cónglín lǐ mí le lù.
examples.english: They got lost in the jungle.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — sound and speech, as in 吃, 唱, 问.
斤 (jīn, axe) is only a loose clue for tīng; the traditional 聽 had 耳 ear.
讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢: to prove by saying.
正 (zhèng) gives the exact sound; 正 also in 整 zhěng and 政 zhèng.
会 (meet, can) — simplified from 會, a lid on a container: bringing things together; hence meeting, then "can" (huì).

example.hanzi: 国会将就这项法案举行听证会。
example.pinyin: guóhuì jiāng jiù zhè xiàng fǎ'àn jǔxíng tīngzhènghuì.
example.english: Congress will hold a hearing on this bill.
example.fact: The 1973 Watergate hearings in the US Senate were broadcast live on television for months, and an estimated 85% of American households tuned in to at least part of the coverage — one of the first times a congressional hearing became mass entertainment.

examples.hanzi: 市政府将举行听证会，听取居民的意见。
examples.pinyin: Shì zhèngfǔ jiāng jǔxíng tīngzhènghuì, tīngqǔ jūmín de yìjiàn.
examples.english: The city government will hold a hearing to listen to residents' opinions.

examples.hanzi: 他在听证会上发了言。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài tīngzhènghuì shàng fā le yán.
examples.english: He spoke at the hearing.

components.note: 木 (tree) — 杰 is simplified from 傑; a tall tree makes a handy picture for an outstanding person standing tall.
西 (west) — traditionally a bird settling on its nest at sunset, hence west; 西 turns up in 要 and 栖.

example.hanzi: 杰西每天早上都去公园跑步。
example.pinyin: jiéxī měitiān zǎoshang dōu qù gōngyuán pǎobù.
example.english: Jesse goes for a run in the park every morning.
example.fact: Sprinter Jesse Owens won four gold medals at the 1936 Berlin Olympics, held under Nazi Germany, directly undermining the regime's propaganda about racial superiority in front of a home crowd of 110,000 spectators.

examples.hanzi: 杰西是我最好的朋友。
examples.pinyin: Jiéxī shì wǒ zuì hǎo de péngyou.
examples.english: Jesse is my best friend.

examples.hanzi: 杰西明天要参加面试。
examples.pinyin: Jiéxī míngtiān yào cānjiā miànshì.
examples.english: Jesse has an interview tomorrow.

components.note: 年 (year) — first drawn as a person carrying harvested grain: one harvest per year. Seen in 今年, 去年, 年轻.
广 (building) — 广 is a building radical, as in 店, 床; 度 also sounds out 渡 dù and 镀 dù.

example.hanzi: 公司即将发布年度财报。
example.pinyin: gōngsī jíjiāng fābù niándù cáibào.
example.english: The company is about to release its annual financial report.
example.fact: The Gregorian calendar, adopted in 1582, adds a leap day nearly every four years to keep pace with Earth's actual orbit of about 365.2422 days — but it skips the leap day in century years not divisible by 400, which is why the year 2000 had one but 1900 and 2100 do not.

examples.hanzi: 这是公司的年度总结会议。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì gōngsī de niándù zǒngjié huìyì.
examples.english: This is the company's annual review meeting.

examples.hanzi: 他获得了年度最佳员工奖。
examples.pinyin: Tā huòdé le niándù zuìjiā yuángōng jiǎng.
examples.english: He won the employee of the year award.

components.note: 刂 (knife) — marks cutting and dividing, as in 别, 刻, 划; 列 is to split into rows, hence a line or list.
歹 (bone, death) — marks death and decay, as in 死, 残; 列 liè itself also sounds out 烈 liè and 裂 liè.
车 (cart) — simplified from 車, a wheeled cart seen from above. As a radical it marks vehicles: 转 turn, 轮 wheel, 较.

example.hanzi: 这辆列车将在十分钟后进站。
example.pinyin: zhè liàng lièchē jiāng zài shí fēnzhōng hòu jìnzhàn.
example.english: This train will arrive at the station in ten minutes.
example.fact: Japan's experimental L0 series maglev train set the world speed record for rail vehicles in 2015, reaching 603 km/h (374 mph) during a test run near Mount Fuji, using magnetic levitation to eliminate friction with the rails.

examples.hanzi: 这趟列车开往北京。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tàng lièchē kāiwǎng Běijīng.
examples.english: This train is heading to Beijing.

examples.hanzi: 列车员正在检查乘客的车票。
examples.pinyin: Lièchēyuán zhèngzài jiǎnchá chéngkè de chēpiào.
examples.english: The train attendant is checking passengers' tickets.

components.note: 钅 (metal, from 金) — marks metals, as in 铁, 钱, 银; 链 is a metal chain.
连 (lián) gives the sound: 链 liàn is close, and 连 also means joined links.

example.hanzi: 她的项链是金子做的。
example.pinyin: Tā de xiàngliàn shì jīnzi zuò de.
example.english: Her necklace is made of gold.
example.fact: 链 is a chain: 项链 (necklace), 锁链, 链条. It became productive in modern speech: 产业链 (industry chain), 供应链 (supply chain), 区块链 (blockchain), and 链接 (a web link).

examples.hanzi: 这条手链是朋友送给我的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo shǒuliàn shì péngyou sòng gěi wǒ de.
examples.english: A friend gave me this bracelet.

examples.hanzi: 自行车的链子掉了。
examples.pinyin: Zìxíngchē de liànzi diào le.
examples.english: The bicycle chain came off.

components.note: 手 (hand) — over 目 (eye): a hand shading the eyes to look into the distance. 目 marks seeing words, as in 眼, 睡.
凵 (open pit) — oldest form shows a foot stepping out of a pit or cave: to go out, come out.

example.hanzi: 我从他的表情看出他很紧张。
example.pinyin: wǒ cóng tā de biǎoqíng kànchū tā hěn jǐnzhāng.
example.english: I could tell from his expression that he was very nervous.
example.fact: Psychologist Paul Ekman's research in the 1960s found that certain facial expressions — for emotions like fear, anger, and surprise — are recognized across vastly different cultures, including isolated tribes in Papua New Guinea who had never seen outside media, suggesting these expressions are biologically innate rather than learned.

examples.hanzi: 你看出我哪里不一样了吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ kàn chū wǒ nǎlǐ bù yíyàng le ma?
examples.english: Can you tell what's different about me?

examples.hanzi: 我看出来他不太高兴。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ kàn chūlái tā bú tài gāoxìng.
examples.english: I could see that he wasn't very happy.

components.note: 木 (tree) — wood, as in 树, 林, 桌: 极 first meant a roof beam, the very top.
及 (jí) gives the exact sound; also in 级 jí and 吸 xī.
其 (its) — an old picture of a winnowing basket (箕 jī adds bamboo). Sound clue: 期 qī, 旗 qí, 棋 qí, 欺 qī, 基 jī.

example.hanzi: 这次考试的题目极其简单。
example.pinyin: Zhè cì kǎoshì de tímù jíqí jiǎndān.
example.english: The questions on this exam were extremely simple.
example.fact: The Mariana Trench's Challenger Deep is the deepest known point in Earth's oceans, plunging to roughly 10,935 meters — deep enough to submerge Mount Everest with more than two kilometers to spare. Only a handful of crewed vehicles have ever reached the bottom, and the pressure there is over 1,000 times that at sea level.

examples.hanzi: 这道菜极其好吃，我吃了两碗饭。
examples.pinyin: Zhè dào cài jíqí hǎochī, wǒ chī le liǎng wǎn fàn.
examples.english: This dish is extremely tasty, and I ate two bowls of rice.

examples.hanzi: 山顶上的风景极其美丽。
examples.pinyin: Shāndǐng shàng de fēngjǐng jíqí měilì.
examples.english: The view from the mountaintop is extremely beautiful.

meanings: respectful form of address for older men

components.note: 师 (shī) is a sound clue for 狮 shī (lion) and 筛 shāi; as a word it means master or teacher.
亻 (person) — a teacher is a person; also in 他 he, 们 plural.
尃 (fū) is a close clue; it also sounds out 博 bó, 簿 bù and 敷 fū.

example.hanzi: 王师傅修车修了三十年了。
example.pinyin: Wáng shīfu xiū chē xiū le sānshí nián le.
example.english: Master Wang has been fixing cars for thirty years.
example.fact: Japanese sushi masters traditionally spend years on preparatory tasks — washing rice, wringing towels, and cooking rice properly — before a mentor lets them touch raw fish, a training path popularized internationally by the documentary Jiro Dreams of Sushi. The apprenticeship model reflects a broader craft tradition where mastery is earned gradually rather than taught directly.

examples.hanzi: 师傅，请问去火车站怎么走？
examples.pinyin: Shīfu, qǐngwèn qù huǒchēzhàn zěnme zǒu?
examples.english: Excuse me, driver, how do I get to the train station?

examples.hanzi: 他跟着老师傅学了三年做菜。
examples.pinyin: Tā gēnzhe lǎo shīfu xué le sān nián zuòcài.
examples.english: He studied cooking under an old master for three years.

components.note: 纟 (thread, simplified 糸) — silk and cord: 红, 给, 组; 线 is thread or line.
戋 (jiān) is a loose sound clue; same part in 浅 qiǎn, 钱 qián and 残 cán.
⻊ (foot, form of 足) — feet and travel: 跑, 跳, 跟; 路 is a road.
各 (gè) is a loose sound clue; same part in 洛 luò, 落 luò, 客 kè.

example.hanzi: 这条线路每天都很堵。
example.pinyin: Zhè tiáo xiànlù měitiān dōu hěn dǔ.
example.english: This route is congested every day.
example.fact: The London Underground's Circle line, opened in 1884, was the world's first underground railway to form a complete loop, and early trains were pulled by steam locomotives that vented smoke into the tunnels — passengers reportedly grew accustomed to breathing sulphurous air on their commute.

examples.hanzi: 这条地铁线路很方便。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo dìtiě xiànlù hěn fāngbiàn.
examples.english: This subway line is very convenient.

examples.hanzi: 电工正在检查家里的线路。
examples.pinyin: Diàngōng zhèngzài jiǎnchá jiālǐ de xiànlù.
examples.english: The electrician is checking the wiring at home.

components.note: 禾 (grain) — 香 originally combined grain with 甘 (sweet): the smell of cooked grain, in modern writing 日 stands in for 甘.
⺼ (flesh, 肉月旁) — body parts, as in 脸 face, 脚 foot, 胖 fat; 肠 is the intestine.
昜 (yáng) is a loose clue; it also sounds out 场 chǎng, 汤 tāng and 扬 yáng.

example.hanzi: 冰箱里还有几根香肠。
example.pinyin: Bīngxiāng lǐ hái yǒu jǐ gēn xiāngcháng.
example.english: There are still a few sausages in the fridge.
example.fact: Sausages are one of the oldest processed foods on record — a Sumerian clay tablet from around 3000 BC already describes meat stuffed into animal intestine casings, a preservation method that let herders store protein long before refrigeration existed.

examples.hanzi: 早餐我想吃香肠和鸡蛋。
examples.pinyin: Zǎocān wǒ xiǎng chī xiāngcháng hé jīdàn.
examples.english: For breakfast I'd like sausage and eggs.

examples.hanzi: 这家店的香肠是自己做的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn de xiāngcháng shì zìjǐ zuò de.
examples.english: The sausages at this shop are homemade.

components.note: 扌 (hand, 提手旁) — hand actions; 拖 is to drag, as in 拉 pull, 推 push.
车 (cart) — simplified from 車, a wheeled cart seen from above. As a radical it marks vehicles: 转 turn, 轮 wheel, 较.

example.hanzi: 他用皮卡拖车把船拖到了湖边。
example.pinyin: Tā yòng píkǎ tuōchē bǎ chuán tuō dào le hú biān.
example.english: He used his pickup truck's tow trailer to haul the boat to the lake.
example.fact: The Bagger 293, a bucket-wheel excavator used in German coal mining, is among the largest land vehicles ever built — about 220 meters long and 96 meters tall — and moves at a walking pace of roughly 10 meters per minute while stripping away hundreds of thousands of tons of earth per day.

examples.hanzi: 我们的车坏了，只能叫拖车。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen de chē huài le, zhǐ néng jiào tuōchē.
examples.english: Our car broke down, so we had to call a tow truck.

examples.hanzi: 这辆拖车可以拖很重的货物。
examples.pinyin: Zhè liàng tuōchē kěyǐ tuō hěn zhòng de huòwù.
examples.english: This trailer can haul very heavy cargo.

components.note: 木 (tree) — wood, as in 树, 林, 桌; the older meaning was a wooden mechanism.
几 (jī) gives the exact sound; also in 饥 jī and 肌 jī.
木 (wood) — early tools were wooden; also in 树 tree, 桌 table.
戒 (jiè) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 诫 jiè.

example.hanzi: 这台机械看起来非常复杂。
example.pinyin: Zhè tái jīxiè kànqǐlái fēicháng fùzá.
example.english: This machine looks extremely complicated.
example.fact: The Antikythera mechanism, recovered from a Greek shipwreck in 1901, is a hand-cranked bronze device built around 150-100 BC that could predict eclipses and track the positions of the sun, moon, and planets — historians consider it the world's oldest known analog computer.

examples.hanzi: 工人们在检修这些机械。
examples.pinyin: Gōngrénmen zài jiǎnxiū zhèxiē jīxiè.
examples.english: The workers are repairing this machinery.

examples.hanzi: 他在一家机械厂工作。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài yì jiā jīxiè chǎng gōngzuò.
examples.english: He works at a machinery factory.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — speech or assent: to say "OK". 可 is also a famous sound part: 河 hé, 歌 gē, 哥 gē, 何 hé all take their sound from it.
乐 (music, joy) — simplified from 樂, a stringed instrument on a wooden stand. Read yuè "music" or lè "joy".

example.hanzi: 他每天午饭都要喝一杯可乐。
example.pinyin: Tā měitiān wǔfàn dōu yào hē yì bēi kělè.
example.english: He drinks a glass of cola with lunch every day.
example.fact: Coca-Cola's original 1886 formula was invented by pharmacist John Pemberton as a patent medicine and, unusually for the era, contained coca leaf extract — a legal ingredient at the time — which the company removed from its recipe around 1903 as attitudes toward the substance shifted.

examples.hanzi: 我想喝一杯冰可乐。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng hē yì bēi bīng kělè.
examples.english: I'd like a glass of iced cola.

examples.hanzi: 汉堡配可乐是很多人的最爱。
examples.pinyin: Hànbǎo pèi kělè shì hěn duō rén de zuì'ài.
examples.english: A burger with cola is a favorite for many people.

components.note: 廾 (two hands) — two hands joined — 共 is doing together; it also sounds out 供 gōng.
广 (building) — 广 is a building radical, as in 店, 床; 度 also sounds out 渡 dù and 镀 dù.

example.hanzi: 我们决定一起共度周末。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen juédìng yìqǐ gòngdù zhōumò.
example.english: We decided to spend the weekend together.
example.fact: Emperor penguins are famous for their extreme cooperative behavior in Antarctica's winter, huddling in tight rotating clusters of thousands of birds to share body heat while temperatures drop below minus 40 degrees Celsius — individuals on the windward edge periodically shuffle toward the warm center so no single bird bears the cold too long.

examples.hanzi: 我们想和家人共度春节。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xiǎng hé jiārén gòngdù Chūnjié.
examples.english: We'd like to spend the Spring Festival with our family.

examples.hanzi: 他们将共度一个难忘的夜晚。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen jiāng gòngdù yí ge nánwàng de yèwǎn.
examples.english: They will spend an unforgettable evening together.

components.note: 纟 (silk, thread) — simplified 糸 (silk thread); early paper was made from silk and fibres, so 纸 sits with 红, 线, 给.
氏 (shì) — only a loose sound hint today — 纸 is zhǐ while 氏 is shì.
木 (wood, tree) — 条 was a long slender twig, so branch, strip, and then the measure word for long things; 木 as in 树, 板.

example.hanzi: 她在门上留了一张纸条。
example.pinyin: Tā zài mén shàng liú le yì zhāng zhǐtiáo.
example.english: She left a note on the door.
example.fact: The Post-it Note was born from a failed adhesive: 3M scientist Spencer Silver created a glue in 1968 that stuck to surfaces but peeled away cleanly, and it took another colleague, Art Fry, several years to realize it was perfect for bookmarks that wouldn't damage the page.

examples.hanzi: 他把电话号码写在纸条上。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ diànhuà hàomǎ xiě zài zhǐtiáo shàng.
examples.english: He wrote the phone number on a slip of paper.

examples.hanzi: 课堂上同学们互相传纸条。
examples.pinyin: Kètáng shàng tóngxuémen hùxiāng chuán zhǐtiáo.
examples.english: Classmates pass notes to each other in class.

components.note: 氵 (water) — dirty water; also in 河 river, 洗 wash.
氵 (water) — 氵 is water — dyeing means soaking in a liquid.
木 (tree, plant) — 木 is the plant dye material, steeped in water to make colour.

example.hanzi: 工厂排放的废水造成了严重污染。
example.pinyin: Gōngchǎng páifàng de fèishuǐ zàochéng le yánzhòng wūrǎn.
example.english: The wastewater discharged by the factory caused severe pollution.
example.fact: The Cuyahoga River in Cleveland caught fire at least a dozen times between the 1860s and 1969 due to industrial pollution and oil slicks on its surface, and the widely publicized 1969 fire helped spur the creation of the US Environmental Protection Agency the following year.

examples.hanzi: 空气污染让很多人感到担心。
examples.pinyin: Kōngqì wūrǎn ràng hěn duō rén gǎndào dānxīn.
examples.english: Air pollution worries many people.

examples.hanzi: 请不要污染我们的河流。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bú yào wūrǎn wǒmen de héliú.
examples.english: Please don't pollute our rivers.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — grabbing and holding; also in 拉 pull, 抓 grab.
句 (jù) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 驹 jū and 钩 gōu.
留 (liú) is a sound clue for 溜 liū, 榴 liú and 瘤 liú; as a word it means to stay or keep.

example.hanzi: 警方将嫌疑人拘留了二十四小时。
example.pinyin: Jǐngfāng jiāng xiányírén jūliú le èrshísì xiǎoshí.
example.english: The police detained the suspect for twenty-four hours.
example.fact: Alcatraz, the notorious island prison in San Francisco Bay, operated as a federal penitentiary from 1934 to 1963 and was chosen partly because the bay's cold currents and strong tides made escape by swimming extremely dangerous, though several inmates still attempted it.

examples.hanzi: 警察拘留了他两天。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngchá jūliú le tā liǎng tiān.
examples.english: The police detained him for two days.

examples.hanzi: 他因为打架被拘留了。
examples.pinyin: Tā yīnwèi dǎjià bèi jūliú le.
examples.english: He was detained for fighting.

components.note: 冫 (ice) — here the ice form of 氵 (water): 决 first meant to break a dam, so a decisive break.
夬 (guài) is a loose sound clue for jué; 夬 also sounds out 快 kuài and 块 kuài.
心 (heart) — a picture of a heart. Written 忄 on the left (快, 怕) and 心 at the bottom (想, 思, 忘); it marks feelings and thoughts.

example.hanzi: 他下定决心要学好英语。
example.pinyin: Tā xiàdìng juéxīn yào xuéhǎo Yīngyǔ.
example.english: He made up his mind to learn English well.
example.fact: Roald Amundsen's team beat Robert Falcon Scott's to the South Pole in 1911 partly through sheer resolve in preparation: Amundsen had spent years studying Inuit survival techniques and relied on sled dogs, while Scott's expedition used motor sledges and ponies that struggled badly in the polar conditions.

examples.hanzi: 我下定决心每天跑步。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiàdìng juéxīn měi tiān pǎobù.
examples.english: I've made up my mind to run every day.

examples.hanzi: 她有决心把这件事做好。
examples.pinyin: Tā yǒu juéxīn bǎ zhè jiàn shì zuò hǎo.
examples.english: She is determined to do this well.

components.note: 土 (earth) — ground and land: 地, 场, 城; hard like packed earth. Top part simplifies 臤 (hard), also in 紧 jǐn and 贤 xián.
亻 (person) — a person and his word: 言 (speech) beside it gives a person who keeps his word, hence "trust, believe".
言 (speech) — written 讠 on the left of other characters, as in 说, 请, 谢.

example.hanzi: 我坚信努力一定会有回报。
example.pinyin: Wǒ jiānxìn nǔlì yídìng huì yǒu huíbào.
example.english: I firmly believe that hard work will pay off.
example.fact: Ignaz Semmelweis, a 19th-century Hungarian physician, firmly believed that unwashed hands were spreading fatal infections in maternity wards, and after he required doctors to wash with a chlorinated solution, mortality rates dropped sharply — yet his peers largely dismissed the idea, and it wasn't widely accepted until decades after his death.

examples.hanzi: 我坚信他会成功。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiānxìn tā huì chénggōng.
examples.english: I firmly believe he will succeed.

examples.hanzi: 大家都坚信明天会更好。
examples.pinyin: Dàjiā dōu jiānxìn míngtiān huì gèng hǎo.
examples.english: Everyone firmly believes tomorrow will be better.

components.note: 尸 (body, shelter) — the top part, as in 层 storey, 居 dwell. 届 is 屆 simplified, meaning 'to arrive', then a term of office (本届).
由 (from, by) — the lower part, standing in for the old shape. The sound yóu does not match jiè, so do not use it as a sound hint.

example.hanzi: 这是我们学校的第一届运动会。
example.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒmen xuéxiào de dì yī jiè yùndònghuì.
example.english: This is our school's first sports meet.
example.fact: 届 counts regular events and graduating classes: 第一届, 本届 (this session), 上一届, and 应届毕业生 (this year's graduates). 届时 means "at that time" in formal announcements.

examples.hanzi: 他是第十五届毕业生。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì dì shíwǔ jiè bìyèshēng.
examples.english: He is a graduate of the fifteenth class.

examples.hanzi: 今年的奥运会是第三十三届。
examples.pinyin: Jīnnián de Àoyùnhuì shì dì sānshísān jiè.
examples.english: This year's Olympics is the thirty-third edition.

components.note: 舟 (boat) — ships, as in 船 ship, 航 sail.
见 (jiàn) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 览 lǎn and 现 xiàn loosely.

example.hanzi: 这艘军舰很大。
example.pinyin: Zhè sōu jūnjiàn hěn dà.
example.english: This warship is very large.
example.fact: 舰 is a naval vessel, counted with 艘: 军舰, 战舰, 航空母舰 (aircraft carrier), 舰队 (fleet). 旗舰 (flagship) has also become a business word, as in 旗舰店 and 旗舰手机.

examples.hanzi: 海边停着一艘大军舰。
examples.pinyin: Hǎibiān tíng zhe yì sōu dà jūnjiàn.
examples.english: A big warship is docked by the sea.

examples.hanzi: 航空母舰是一种很大的军舰。
examples.pinyin: Hángkōng mǔjiàn shì yì zhǒng hěn dà de jūnjiàn.
examples.english: An aircraft carrier is a very large kind of warship.

components.note: 力 (strength) — effort, as in 办, 男, 努; 助 is to lend strength.
且 (qiě) is a loose sound clue for zhù; 且 also sounds out 祖 zǔ, 租 zū and 姐 jiě.

example.hanzi: 谢谢你帮助我。
example.pinyin: Xièxie nǐ bāngzhù wǒ.
example.english: Thank you for helping me.
example.fact: 助 is mostly found in compounds: 帮助, 协助, 助手 (assistant), 助理, 互助 (mutual aid). In sports, 助攻 is an assist. 助 sounds more formal than the everyday verb 帮.

examples.hanzi: 他经常助人为乐。
examples.pinyin: Tā jīngcháng zhùrénwéilè.
examples.english: He often finds joy in helping others.

examples.hanzi: 你有问题可以找我帮助。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yǒu wèntí kěyǐ zhǎo wǒ bāngzhù.
examples.english: If you have a problem, you can ask me for help.

components.note: 刂 (knife, 立刀旁) — cutting and sharp action, as in 别, 利, 剪.
杀 (shā) gives the exact sound.
车 (cart) — simplified from 車, a wheeled cart seen from above. As a radical it marks vehicles: 转 turn, 轮 wheel, 较.

example.hanzi: 司机猛地刹车,车上的人都晃了一下。
example.pinyin: Sījī měngde shāchē, chē shàng de rén dōu huàng le yíxià.
example.english: The driver slammed on the brakes, and everyone in the car lurched.
example.fact: Antilock braking systems (ABS), now standard on most cars, were first developed for aircraft in the 1950s to prevent wheels from locking up on landing, and the technology only migrated to passenger vehicles in the 1970s once electronic sensors became cheap and reliable enough.

examples.hanzi: 前面有人，快刹车！
examples.pinyin: Qiánmiàn yǒu rén, kuài shāchē!
examples.english: There's someone ahead, brake quickly!

examples.hanzi: 这辆车的刹车有点儿问题。
examples.pinyin: Zhè liàng chē de shāchē yǒudiǎnr wèntí.
examples.english: There's a small problem with this car's brakes.

components.note: 人 (person) — one person following another: 从 means to follow, then "from".
彐 (hand-like part) — 事 is usually explained as a hand holding a tool or tally, 'handling business' — a hedged reading, not certain.
史 (history, scribe) — shares an ancient root with 事: a hand holding a recording tool. Both are about handling official 'matters'.

example.hanzi: 他大学毕业后一直从事教育工作。
example.pinyin: Tā dàxué bìyè hòu yìzhí cóngshì jiàoyù gōngzuò.
example.english: Since graduating from university, he has worked in education.
example.fact: Before becoming a full-time author, Stan Lee spent years writing comics for what was then Timely Comics under various pseudonyms, and it wasn't until 1961, with the launch of the Fantastic Four, that he and artist Jack Kirby began building the shared universe that became Marvel Comics.

examples.hanzi: 他从事软件开发已经五年了。
examples.pinyin: Tā cóngshì ruǎnjiàn kāifā yǐjīng wǔ nián le.
examples.english: He has been engaged in software development for five years.

examples.hanzi: 她想从事医疗工作。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎng cóngshì yīliáo gōngzuò.
examples.english: She wants to work in the medical field.

components.note: 亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 住.
立 (stand) — the spot where a person 亻 stands 立: a position or seat; also 位置 position.
于 (yú) is a sound clue for 宇 yǔ and 芋 yù; it is a light grammar word meaning "at, to".

example.hanzi: 这座图书馆位于市中心。
example.pinyin: Zhè zuò túshūguǎn wèiyú shì zhōngxīn.
example.english: This library is located in the city center.
example.fact: The Library of Alexandria, founded in Egypt around the 3rd century BC, is estimated to have held several hundred thousand papyrus scrolls at its peak and employed scholars tasked with collecting a copy of every known text in the ancient world — its eventual loss remains one of history's most-cited cultural tragedies, though the exact cause is still debated.

examples.hanzi: 我们的学校位于一条安静的街上。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen de xuéxiào wèiyú yì tiáo ānjìng de jiē shàng.
examples.english: Our school is located on a quiet street.

examples.hanzi: 这座城市位于海边。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò chéngshì wèiyú hǎibiān.
examples.english: This city is situated by the sea.

components.note: 马 (horse) — a galloping horse. As a radical it marks horses: 骑 ride, 驾 drive. It gives sound to 妈 mā, 吗 ma, 骂 mà and 码 mǎ.
戈 (halberd) — weapons, as in 战 war and 成; the traditional 戲 was a play or contest.
囗 (enclosure) — boundaries: 国, 园, 围; 团 is a round group. Its traditional form had 專 as sound, like 转 zhuǎn and 传 chuán.

example.hanzi: 孩子们都很期待马戏团的表演。
example.pinyin: Háizimen dōu hěn qídài mǎxìtuán de biǎoyǎn.
example.english: The children are all looking forward to the circus performance.
example.fact: Ringling Bros. and Barnum & Bailey Circus, once billed as 'The Greatest Show on Earth,' operated continuously from 1871 until it closed in 2017 after 146 years, a shutdown driven partly by declining ticket sales following its 2016 decision to retire its famous elephant acts.

examples.hanzi: 周末我们带孩子去看马戏团表演。
examples.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒmen dài háizi qù kàn mǎxìtuán biǎoyǎn.
examples.english: On the weekend we take the kids to watch a circus show.

examples.hanzi: 马戏团的小丑逗得大家哈哈大笑。
examples.pinyin: Mǎxìtuán de xiǎochǒu dòu de dàjiā hāhā dà xiào.
examples.english: The circus clown made everyone burst out laughing.

components.note: 亻 (person) — person radical — 传 is something passed from person to person.
专 (zhuān) — near sound — 传 is chuán; 专 also sounds out 转 zhuǎn and 砖 zhuān.
扌 (hand) — hand radical — 播 is scattering seed by hand, then broadcasting.
番 (fān) — near sound — 播 is bō; 番 also sounds out 翻 fān and 潘 pān.

example.hanzi: 这个消息很快就在网上传播开了。
example.pinyin: Zhège xiāoxi hěn kuài jiù zài wǎngshàng chuánbō kāi le.
example.english: This news quickly spread online.
example.fact: The 1918 influenza pandemic is estimated to have infected roughly a third of the world's population and killed at least 50 million people, spreading rapidly along the troop movements and crowded conditions of the final months of World War I — a pattern epidemiologists still study when modeling how diseases travel through connected populations.

examples.hanzi: 病毒通过空气传播。
examples.pinyin: Bìngdú tōngguò kōngqì chuánbō.
examples.english: The virus spreads through the air.

examples.hanzi: 好的习惯会在家庭里传播。
examples.pinyin: Hǎo de xíguàn huì zài jiātíng lǐ chuánbō.
examples.english: Good habits spread within a family.

components.note: 母 (mǔ) is a close sound clue for měi; the same part also in 海 hǎi, 梅 méi and 悔 huǐ.
當 (traditional) — 田 field under 尚 (shàng), 尚 being a loose sound hint for dāng. 当 keeps only a squashed top and a few strokes of it.
尚 (shàng) — the top part of 當; only a loose sound clue today. 当 is dāng (to act as, should) or dàng (appropriate).

example.hanzi: 每当下雨,他就会想起家乡。
example.pinyin: Měidāng xiàyǔ, tā jiù huì xiǎngqǐ jiāxiāng.
example.english: Whenever it rains, he thinks of his hometown.
example.fact: Petrichor, the distinctive earthy smell after rain, comes partly from geosmin, a compound produced by soil-dwelling bacteria called actinomycetes — human noses are remarkably sensitive to it, able to detect concentrations as low as a few parts per trillion.

examples.hanzi: 每当夜晚来临，他就会拉小提琴。
examples.pinyin: Měidāng yèwǎn láilín, tā jiù huì lā xiǎotíqín.
examples.english: Whenever night falls, he plays the violin.

examples.hanzi: 每当我难过的时候，朋友都会陪着我。
examples.pinyin: Měidāng wǒ nánguò de shíhou, péngyou dōu huì péizhe wǒ.
examples.english: Every time I feel down, my friends keep me company.

components.note: 幸 (luck) — often read as an old picture of shackles; 'luck' is escaping punishment. The dictionary story (one alive 土, one dead 干) is a memory aid.
土 (earth) — the top. Memory aid: the one standing on solid ground 土 is the lucky one — 幸运, 幸福.
女 (woman) — women and family, as in 妈, 她, 姐.
子 (child) — a woman with her child: the picture of something good.

example.hanzi: 幸好他带了雨伞,不然就淋湿了。
example.pinyin: Xìnghǎo tā dài le yǔsǎn, bùrán jiù línshī le.
example.english: Luckily he brought an umbrella, or he would have gotten soaked.
example.fact: In 1943, engineer Richard James accidentally invented the Slinky when a torsion spring he was developing to stabilize ship equipment fell off a shelf and 'walked' across the floor instead of just clattering down — a lucky mishap that became one of the best-selling toys of the 20th century.

examples.hanzi: 幸好我们提前出发了，没有迟到。
examples.pinyin: Xìnghǎo wǒmen tíqián chūfā le, méiyǒu chídào.
examples.english: Luckily we set off early and weren't late.

examples.hanzi: 幸好没人受伤。
examples.pinyin: Xìnghǎo méi rén shòushāng.
examples.english: Fortunately, nobody was hurt.

components.note: 衣 (clothing) — cutting cloth to make clothes; also as 衤 in 衬, 被.
戈 (spear) — the cutting blade; also in 战 war, 或 or.
刂 (knife) — 刂 is 刀 (knife) as in 到, 别, 利; 判 is to cut in half, so to separate and decide.
半 (bàn) — near sound — 判 is pàn; 半 means half.

example.hanzi: 裁判判他犯规,取消了这个球。
example.pinyin: Cáipàn pàn tā fànguī, qǔxiāo le zhège qiú.
example.english: The referee ruled it a foul and disallowed the goal.
example.fact: Goal-line technology in soccer, which uses multiple high-speed cameras to determine within millimeters whether a ball has fully crossed the line, was first used at a major tournament in the 2014 World Cup — a response to decades of contested goals that referees on the pitch simply couldn't see clearly enough.

examples.hanzi: 足球比赛需要三名裁判。
examples.pinyin: Zúqiú bǐsài xūyào sān míng cáipàn.
examples.english: A soccer match needs three referees.

examples.hanzi: 他对裁判的决定不满意。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì cáipàn de juédìng bù mǎnyì.
examples.english: He was unhappy with the referee's decision.

components.note: 冏 (bright/window) — the lower part; dictionary treats it as the 'bright' hint. Meaning 'trade, business' is better remembered as a market (商店).
口 (mouth) — dictionary radical, as in 吃 eat. Memory aid: a shop-keeper's mouth calling out prices; 商量 is to 'talk it over'.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.hanzi: 他是当地很有名的商人。
example.pinyin: Tā shì dāngdì hěn yǒumíng de shāngrén.
example.english: He is a well-known businessman in the local area.
example.fact: The Medici family rose from relatively modest origins in 14th-century Florence to become one of Europe's most powerful banking dynasties, and their wealth from trade and finance directly funded much of the early Italian Renaissance, including commissions to artists like Michelangelo and Botticelli.

examples.hanzi: 那位商人在全国开了很多家店。
examples.pinyin: Nà wèi shāngrén zài quánguó kāi le hěn duō jiā diàn.
examples.english: That businessman has opened many shops across the country.

examples.hanzi: 古代的商人经常走丝绸之路。
examples.pinyin: Gǔdài de shāngrén jīngcháng zǒu sīchóu zhī lù.
examples.english: Merchants in ancient times often traveled the Silk Road.

components.note: 大 (big) — a front-facing person with arms and legs spread wide: big. As radical, 大 is in 天 sky, 太 too much, 夫 man.
⺼ (flesh, 肉月旁) — the body-part radical, as in 脸, 腿, 脑; 胆 is the gall bladder, then courage.
旦 (dàn) hints at the sound: 胆 dǎn is close to 担 dān and 但 dàn.

example.hanzi: 他竟然大胆地在会上提出反对意见。
example.pinyin: Tā jìngrán dàdǎn de zài huì shàng tíchū fǎnduì yìjiàn.
example.english: He boldly raised his objection in the meeting.
example.fact: In 1911, art thief Vincenzo Peruggia walked out of the Louvre with the Mona Lisa hidden under his coat during regular opening hours, simply by hiding overnight in a supply closet — the painting was missing for over two years before he was caught trying to sell it in Italy.

examples.hanzi: 这个想法很大胆，但很有创意。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xiǎngfǎ hěn dàdǎn, dàn hěn yǒu chuàngyì.
examples.english: This idea is bold but very creative.

examples.hanzi: 你就大胆地试一试吧。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ jiù dàdǎn de shì yi shì ba.
examples.english: Go ahead and give it a bold try.

components.note: 隹 (short-tailed bird) — bird element as in 难, 谁, 集; in 雇 it is historical, so just treat it as a part.
户 (hù) — sounds out 雇 gù — close (same final, h→g); 户 also sounds out 顾 gù, so 雇 and 顾 sound alike.
用 (use) — early picture is debated: a pail, a fenced enclosure or a hung bell. Memory aid: a door-frame 冂 with a cross-bar — a tool 'put to use' (使用, 不用).

example.hanzi: 这家公司准备雇用十名新员工。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī zhǔnbèi gùyòng shí míng xīn yuángōng.
example.english: This company is planning to hire ten new employees.
example.fact: The Ford Motor Company's decision in 1914 to pay assembly-line workers five dollars a day — roughly double the prevailing wage — was initially seen as reckless by other industrialists, but it sharply cut worker turnover and let employees afford the very cars they were building.

examples.hanzi: 这家餐厅雇用了很多年轻人。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā cāntīng gùyòng le hěn duō niánqīngrén.
examples.english: This restaurant employs many young people.

examples.hanzi: 我们不雇用没有经验的人。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen bù gùyòng méiyǒu jīngyàn de rén.
examples.english: We don't hire people without experience.

components.note: 欠 (yawn, open mouth) — 欠 shows a person with an open mouth, as in 吹 blow, 欢 joyful; 歌 is the mouth opened in song.
哥 (gē) — same sound — 歌 is gē, just like 哥; 哥 means elder brother.
口 (mouth) — mouth radical for speaking and sounds, as in 吃, 叫, 吗; 唱 is to sing.
昌 (chāng) — same sound, different tone — 唱 is chàng; 昌 also sounds out 倡 chàng.

example.hanzi: 孩子们围在一起歌唱。
example.pinyin: Háizimen wéi zài yìqǐ gēchàng.
example.english: The children gathered together and sang.
example.fact: Humpback whale songs, which can last up to 30 minutes and repeat in structured phrases, are thought to spread between populations like cultural trends — researchers have tracked entirely new songs originating off Australia and spreading eastward across the Pacific over several years.

examples.hanzi: 她喜欢一边做饭一边歌唱。
examples.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan yìbiān zuòfàn yìbiān gēchàng.
examples.english: She likes singing while she cooks.

examples.hanzi: 鸟儿在树上欢快地歌唱。
examples.pinyin: Niǎor zài shù shàng huānkuài de gēchàng.
examples.english: Birds sing cheerfully in the trees.

components.note: 鬲 (cooking cauldron) — steam rising from a pot, things heating and blending; 虫 (chóng) is only a loose sound clue.
入 (enter) — a pointed shape pushing in; not 人 (person), whose strokes spread outward.

example.hanzi: 新来的同事很快就融入了团队。
example.pinyin: Xīn lái de tóngshì hěn kuài jiù róngrù le tuánduì.
example.english: The new colleague quickly integrated into the team.
example.fact: Coral reefs form through a close partnership between coral polyps and microscopic algae called zooxanthellae, which live inside the coral's tissue and photosynthesize sunlight into food; when ocean temperatures rise, corals expel these algae in a stress response known as bleaching, often leading to reef death.

examples.hanzi: 他很快就融入了新的班级。
examples.pinyin: Tā hěn kuài jiù róngrù le xīn de bānjí.
examples.english: He quickly fit into his new class.

examples.hanzi: 颜色应该融入整个画面。
examples.pinyin: Yánsè yīnggāi róngrù zhěng ge huàmiàn.
examples.english: The colors should blend into the whole picture.

components.note: 艹 (plants) — marks grasses and flowers, as in 草, 茶, 菜; 花 is a flower.
化 (huà) hints at the sound: 花 huā is close, and 化 also gives 华 huá and 货 huò.
钅 (metal) — 钅 is the simplified 金 (metal), as in 铁, 银, 钟; early money was metal coins.
戋 (jiān) — near sound — 钱 is qián; 戋 also sounds out 浅 qiǎn and 线 xiàn, and means small or thin.

example.hanzi: 他一到周末就喜欢出去花钱。
example.pinyin: Tā yí dào zhōumò jiù xǐhuān chūqù huāqián.
example.english: As soon as the weekend arrives, he likes to go out and spend money.
example.fact: Lydia, an ancient kingdom in what is now western Turkey, is generally credited with minting the world's first standardized metal coins around the 7th century BC, made from electrum, a naturally occurring alloy of gold and silver.

examples.hanzi: 这个月我花钱太多了。
examples.pinyin: Zhège yuè wǒ huāqián tài duō le.
examples.english: I spent too much money this month.

examples.hanzi: 他不喜欢在衣服上花钱。
examples.pinyin: Tā bù xǐhuan zài yīfu shàng huāqián.
examples.english: He doesn't like spending money on clothes.

components.note: 辶 (movement, road) — 辶 marks going and moving, as in 过, 进, 逃; 避 is stepping aside.
辟 (bì) — same sound — 避 is bì, like 辟; 辟 also sounds out 壁 bì and 臂 bì.
廾 (two hands) — in 開 two hands lift the bar of a gate; 开 is the simplified shape. Compare 关 (close).

example.hanzi: 他绕了远路,想避开堵车。
example.pinyin: Tā rào le yuǎnlù, xiǎng bìkāi dǔchē.
example.english: He took a longer route to avoid the traffic jam.
example.fact: Migratory birds such as bar-tailed godwits can detect approaching storms through changes in barometric pressure and will delay or reroute multi-thousand-kilometer flights to avoid flying directly into severe weather over open ocean, where there is nowhere to land and rest.

examples.hanzi: 你得避开中午最热的时候出门。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ děi bìkāi zhōngwǔ zuì rè de shíhou chūmén.
examples.english: You should avoid going out during the hottest part of noon.

examples.hanzi: 他故意避开了我的目光。
examples.pinyin: Tā gùyì bìkāi le wǒ de mùguāng.
examples.english: He deliberately avoided my gaze.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — a house, as in 家, 安, 室; 宽 is a roomy house, hence wide and generous.

example.hanzi: 这条马路很宽。
example.pinyin: Zhè tiáo mǎlù hěn kuān.
example.english: This road is very wide.
example.fact: 宽 describes width (opposite of 窄), but also leniency: 宽容 (tolerant), 宽松 (loose), 放宽 (to relax rules). 宽带 means broadband, and "three meters wide" is 三米宽.

examples.hanzi: 这条河有五十米宽。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo hé yǒu wǔshí mǐ kuān.
examples.english: This river is fifty meters wide.

examples.hanzi: 这个房间很宽敞，也很明亮。
examples.pinyin: Zhège fángjiān hěn kuānchang, yě hěn míngliàng.
examples.english: This room is spacious and bright.
